```text
## SpecStory CLI

SpecStory CLI is a cross-platform command-line tool for saving AI coding coversations from terminal coding agents (e.g. Claude Code, Cursor CLI, Codex CLI, Gemini CLI, Droid CLI, etc.).

It saves your AI coding conversations as local markdown files of each session. It can optionally sync your markdown files to the [SpecStory Cloud](https://cloud.specstory.com), turning your AI chat history into a centralized knowledge system that you can chat with and search.

## Features

- Cross-platform support (Linux, macOS)
- Seamless integration with terminal coding agents
- Command-line wrapper for terminal coding agents with markdown auto-save
- Sync all your prior conversations to local markdown files
- Optional: Syncs your markdown files to the SpecStory Cloud for easy search and chat
- Open source under the Apache 2.0 license

## Agent Support

The following coding agents are supported in the SpecStory CLI:

| Agent                                                     | Provider                                  | Data Format | Source Location         |
|-----------------------------------------------------------|-------------------------------------------|-------------|-------------------------|
| [Claude Code](https://www.claude.com/product/claude-code) | [claudecode](pkg/providers/claudecode/)   | JSONL       | `~/.claude/projects/`   |
| [Codex CLI](https://www.openai.com/codex/cli/)            | [codexcli](pkg/providers/codexcli/)       | JSONL       | `~/.codex/sessions/`    |
| [Cursor CLI](https://cursor.com/cli)                      | [cursorcli](pkg/providers/cursorcli/)     | SQLite      | `~/.cursor/chats/`      |
| [Droid CLI](https://factory.ai/product/cli)               | [droidcli](pkg/providers/droidcli/)       | JSONL       | `~/.factory/sessions/`  |
--
```

Syncing all files for the current project:

```zsh
# Defaults to syncing for all providers if no provider is specified
specstory sync <provider>
```

With a specific session UUID:

```zsh
specstory sync -s <session-uuid>
```

### Skills

SpecStory Cloud mines your synced sessions into reusable skills. The `skills` command lets you browse, approve, and install them into your coding agents. It requires a SpecStory Cloud login (`specstory login`) and a Pro plan.

```zsh
# Interactive browser with two tabs (press `tab` to switch):
#   • Library — preview skills, approve/reject those awaiting review, install ready
#     ones, and uninstall/reinstall installed ones.
#   • Run Activity — see past runs, kick one off (`n`), and watch it live.
specstory skills
```

Skills install using the same layout as the public `npx skills` CLI: a canonical
`~/.agents/skills/<name>` store, symlinked into each detected agent's skills directory
(Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, and more), tracked in the shared `~/.agents/.skill-lock.json`.
Installs default to global; pass `--project` to install into the current repo instead.

Every action is also a non-interactive subcommand with `--json`, so a front end (e.g. the
VS Code extension) can drive the same engine:

```zsh
specstory skills list --json                 # browse the library + local install state
specstory skills show <name>                 # print a skill's SKILL.md
specstory skills approve <name>              # approve a skill awaiting review
specstory skills reject <name> --note "..."  # reject one
specstory skills install <name>              # install for all detected agents (global)
specstory skills install <name> --project --agents claude-code,codex
specstory skills uninstall <name>            # remove files, links, and lock entry
specstory skills reinstall <name>            # refresh to the current cloud version
specstory skills status --json               # locally installed skills (no login needed)
specstory skills run                         # mine your sessions for new skills
specstory skills runs --json                 # recent runs and their status
```

To generate new skills, kick off a run (`specstory skills run`, or press `n` in the browser to
watch it live). Runs mine your synced sessions in the cloud and take a few minutes.

### Targeting a non-production cloud

By default the CLI talks to `https://cloud.specstory.com`. To point every command at a
dev/staging cloud without passing `--cloud-url` each time, set an environment variable:

```zsh
export SPECSTORY_CLOUD_URL=https://cloud-dev.specstory.com
specstory login   # authenticate against that cloud
specstory skills  # ...and everything else now uses it
```

Resolution order is `--cloud-url` flag → `SPECSTORY_CLOUD_URL` → production default, so a
one-off `--cloud-url` still wins for a single command. `login` prints the target host when it
isn't production, so you always know which cloud you're authenticating against.

## Configuration File

SpecStory CLI supports configuration files in TOML format. Settings can be configured at two levels:

1. **User-level config**: `~/.specstory/cli/config.toml` - applies to all projects
2. **Project-level config**: `.specstory/cli/config.toml` - applies only to the current project
```

652	// projectIDCache memoizes ComputeProjectID by cwd, since many sessions share a cwd and
653	// each resolution walks the filesystem to the git root.
654	type projectIDCache struct {
655		mu sync.Mutex
656		m  map[string]projectIDName
657	}
658	
659	func (c *projectIDCache) resolve(cwd string) (string, string) {
660		if strings.TrimSpace(cwd) == "" {
661			return unknownProjectID, ""
662		}
663		c.mu.Lock()
664		defer c.mu.Unlock()
665		if v, ok := c.m[cwd]; ok {
666			return v.id, v.name
667		}
668		id, name, err := utils.ComputeProjectID(cwd)
669		if err != nil || id == "" {
670			id, name = unknownProjectID, ""
671		}
672		c.m[cwd] = projectIDName{id, name}
673		return id, name
674	}
675	
676	// ---- helpers ----
677	
678	// summarizeCounts renders "claude 683 · codex 70 · …" in registry order, omitting zeros.
679	func summarizeCounts(ids []string, totals map[string]int) string {
680		var parts []string
681		for _, id := range ids {
682			if totals[id] > 0 {
683				parts = append(parts, fmt.Sprintf("%s %d", id, totals[id]))
684			}
685		}
686		return strings.Join(parts, " · ")
687	}
688	
689	// ---- live progress (per-agent bars) ----
690	
691	// reindexProgress renders live per-agent progress. Workers bump atomic per-agent
692	// counters and observe project ids; a single render goroutine redraws the block in
693	// place on a TTY (ANSI cursor-up), or prints periodic plain lines otherwise. No worker
694	// draws directly. See docs/SESSIONS-DB.md "Reindex Progress UX".
695	type reindexProgress struct {
696		agents []string          // agents with >0 sessions, in registry order
697		totals map[string]int    // per-agent session totals
698		done   map[string]*int64 // per-agent completed counters (atomic)
699		tty    bool
700

```text
1	# Supabase Schema Usage Analysis
2	
3	This note summarizes the SpecStory Cloud schema as implemented in the repo and explains how to use the companion SQL workbook:
4	
5	- [supabase-cloud-usage-queries.sql](./supabase-cloud-usage-queries.sql)
6	
7	## Sources Read
8	
9	- `supabase/schema.sql`
10	- `supabase/migrations/*.sql`
11	- `shared/db/schema.ts`
12	- `shared/database.types.ts`
13	- `shared/types.ts`
14	- `README.md`
15	- `ARCHITECTURE.md`
16	- `DEVICE-AUTH.md`
17	- `docs/2026-02-07_user-data-deletion.md`
18	- `sync-cloud/worker/handlers/*.ts`
19	- `shared/models/*.ts`
20	- `workers/*/src/*.ts`
21	
22	`shared/db/schema.ts` plus `shared/database.types.ts` appear more current than `supabase/schema.sql`. The SQL workbook targets the effective current schema from those files.
23	
24	## Mental Model
25	
26	SpecStory Cloud stores synced AI coding history as:
27	
28	```text
29	workspaces
30	  -> sessions
31	    -> exchanges
32	      -> exchange_chunks
33	        -> chunk_embeddings
34	```
35	
36	The product also stores:
37	
38	- access and identity helpers: `user_permissions`, `api_tokens`, `device_auth_codes`, `device_refresh_tokens`
39	- RAG chat usage: `rag_chat_sessions`, `rag_chat_messages`, `rag_chat_message_chunks`, `rag_chat_messages_workspaces`
40	- search/summary helpers: `user_exchange_search`, `workspace_sessions_summary`
41	
42	## Important Identifier Rules
43	
44	- `workspaces.id` is the internal cloud UUID.
45	- `workspaces.project_id` is client-generated from the local project/repo/directory.
46	- `workspaces.owner_id` is the Clerk user id for the owner.
47	- `sessions.id` is the internal cloud UUID.
48	- `sessions.client_id` is the client session id used by the public API.
49	- `user_permissions.user_id` is a Clerk user id that has access to a workspace.
50	
51	This matters because many analytics questions should group by `owner_id`, but API/debug questions often need `client_id`.
52	
53	## What The Major Tables Mean
54	
55	`workspaces`: one cloud-side project workspace for a user and client project id. Current code creates/upserts by `(project_id, owner_id)`.
56	
57	`sessions`: a synced SpecStory session. Stores markdown content, raw-data size, metadata, share state, timestamps, and a `should_skip_processing` flag.
58	
59	`exchanges`: parsed user/assistant exchange chunks from session markdown. Full-text search runs here via `fts`.
60	
61	`exchange_chunks` and `chunk_embeddings`: vector-search source material generated after exchanges are parsed. RAG chat searches these rows.
62	
63	`rag_chat_sessions` and `rag_chat_messages`: user questions to SpecStory Cloud chat and generated responses. Message metadata includes rewritten queries, context chunk counts, projects searched, and optional time filters.
64	
65	`rag_chat_message_chunks`: citations from a chat response back to chunks/sessions/workspaces.
66	
67	`device_auth_codes` and `device_refresh_tokens`: CLI/IDE device-login funnel and long-lived device auth.
68	
69	`api_tokens`: programmatic API keys, scopes, last-used tracking, and revocation state.
70	
71	## Metadata Fields Worth Querying
72	
73	Session metadata currently includes:
74	
75	- `clientName`
76	- `clientVersion`
77	- `agentName`
78	- `deviceId`
79	- `gitBranches`
80	- `llmModels`
81	- `tags`
82	- `markdownVersion`
83	- `summary`
84	- `summaryGeneratedAt`
85	
86	Exchange metadata currently includes:
87	
88	- `summary`
89	- `summaryGeneratedAt`
90	
91	RAG chat message metadata currently includes:
92	
93	- `rewritten_query`
94	- `context_chunks`
95	- `projects_searched`
96	- `time_filter`
97	
98	## Recommended Query Order
99	
100	Start with:
101	
102	1. Schema inventory: queries 1 to 5.
103	2. Product snapshot: query 6.
104	3. Workspace/project shape: queries 7 and 8.
105	4. Core usage: queries 9 to 16.
106	5. Worker health: queries 17 and 18.
107	6. RAG/chat usage: queries 20 to 24.
108	7. Auth and API adoption: queries 25 to 29.
109	
110	Query 24 and query 30 return user-entered content excerpts. Run them only when you intentionally want content-level inspection.
111
```

```text
CREATE OR REPLACE VIEW workspace_sessions_summary AS
SELECT 
  w.id,
  w.project_id,
  w.owner_id,
  w.name,
  w.icon,
  w.color,
  w.created_at,
  w.updated_at,
  COUNT(s.id) as session_count,
  MAX(s.updated_at) as last_session,
  COALESCE(SUM(s.markdown_size), 0) as total_markdown_size
FROM workspaces w
LEFT JOIN sessions s ON w.id = s.workspace_id
GROUP BY w.id, w.project_id, w.owner_id, w.name, w.icon, w.color, w.created_at, w.updated_at;
```

```text
1	# Project Identity
2	
3	On extension activation, if Auto-save is enabled, AFTER we create the `.specstory` directory (if it didn't already exist) create a `.specstory/.project.json` file to capture project identity ONLY if the file doesn't already exist.
4	
5	The file will always have a `workspace_id` key, and will sometimes have a `git_id` key. If the file already exists, do check it for the presence of a `git_id` and ONLY if there isn't one, see if we can now give it one.
6	
7	```json
8	{
9	  "workspace_id": "hash",
10	  "workspace_id_at": ISO-8601-timestamp,
11	  "git_id": "hash",
12	  "git_id_at": ISO-8601-timestamp,
13	}
14	```
15	
16	`git_id` is a repeatable hash from the url for the remote called "origin" from the .git/config (if present). If it's not present, there is no `git_id` key. The same remote "origin" will has the same `git_id`.
17	
18	GitHub HTTPS clone:
19	
20	```
21	[remote "origin"]
22		url = https://github.com/patterns-ai-core/langchainrb.git
23	```
24	
25	GitHub SSH clone:
26	
27	```
28	[remote "origin"]
29		url = git@github.com:patterns-ai-core/langchainrb.git
30	```
31	
32	Other service clone (made up example):
33	
34	```
35	[remote "origin"]
36		url = git@gitlab.com:patterns-ai-core/langchainrb.git
37	```
38	
39	We want these first 2 GitHub cases to give us the same hash, no matter if the user happens to clone via HTTPS or SSH, so look for and remove `https://github.com/` and `git@github.com:` if they are present in the URL before using it as a hash. If neither of those strings is present, like in the 3rd example, just use the whole URL as the hash that creates the `git_id`.
40	
41	`workspace_id` is a repeatable hash from the full path of the cwd that the SpecStory CLI was run from. The same cwd will hash to the same `worskpace_id`.
42	
43	## Reason for these IDs
44	
45	We are looking for "project persistence" that's resiliant.
46	
47	ID saves us from user moving/renaming the project directory. That's OK cause the `workspace_id` stays the same, it's been persisted to the `.specstory/.project.json` file.
48	
49	The git ID provides a potentially even more resiliant ID, in the case of:
50	- User remove .specstory/
51	- With Git User can move/rename the workspace and then remove .specstory (with the same git origin)
52	- User has the same project in multiple devices, or places on the same device
53	- Multiple users have the same project on their devices
54	
55	Despite our attempts here, the user is still SOL in the case of:
56	- Without Git User can move/rename/modify the workspace and then remove .specstory
57	- With Git User can move/rename/modify the workspace and then change the git origin and remove .specstory
58	(in the future for these SOL cases, we can use interaction with the user to reidentity the project)
59
```
</details></tool-use>

1	# SpecStory Cloud
2	
3	AI Agent History in the Cloud, web application and API, built with Cloudflare Workers and Supabase.
4	
5	## Overview
6	
7	The API provides a REST interface for CRUD of AI agent session data, including the markdown content and raw data. A GraphQL API supports full-text search and filtering.
8	
9	The service uses Supabase for database storage and file storage. Cloudflare Workers power a public API and various data derivation workers. Vite and Turbo are used for the build system. The web application is a React SPA that uses the public API. User authentication is via Clerk, with API authentication and authorization via JWTokens.
10	
11	## Table of Contents
12	
13	- [SpecStory Cloud](#specstory-cloud)
14	  - [Overview](#overview)
15	  - [Table of Contents](#table-of-contents)

39	
40	## Quick Start
41	
42	### Prerequisites
43	
44	- Node.js 18+
45	- Docker (for Supabase local development)
46	
47	### Installation & Setup
48	
49	1. **Clone and install dependencies:**
50	
51	```bash
52	git clone <repository-url>
53	cd specstory-sync
54	npm install
55	```
56	
57	2. **Set up environment variables:**
58	
59	```bash
60	# Copy the example environment file
61	cp .env.example .env.development
62	
63	# Edit .env.development with your actual values
64	# See Environment Configuration section below for details
65	```
66	
67	3. **Start the application:**
68	
69	```bash
70	# This will start both Supabase and the frontend concurrently
71	npm run dev
72	```
73	
74	The application will be available at:
75	
76	- **Frontend**: http://localhost:5173
77	
78	Web UI access to the database will be available at:
79	
80	- **Supabase Studio**: http://localhost:54323
81	
82	All API endpoints will be available at:
83	
84	- **API**: http://localhost:5173/api/v1/\* (proxied through Vite)
85	
86	## Environment Configuration
87	
88	### Local Development (.env.development)
89	
90	Copy `.env.example` to `.env.development` and needed variables documented within the example file.
91	
92	### Getting Environment Values
93	
94	**Supabase Keys (after running `npm run dev:supabase`):**
95	
96	- The Supabase keys will be displayed in the terminal output
97	- Copy the `anon key` and `service_role key` from the startup logs
98	
99	**Clerk Keys:**
100	
101	- Sign up at [clerk.com](https://clerk.com)
102	- Create a new application
103	- Get your publishable key, secret key, and JWT key from the Clerk dashboard
104	
105	**JWT Secret:**
106	
107	- Generate a secure random string (32+ characters)
108	- Used for signing custom JWT tokens
109	
110	**Faking your subscription plan (local dev only):**
111	
112	- Set `DEV_FAKE_PLAN=pro` (or `team` / `enterprise` / `free`) in `.env.development` to treat any signed-in user as that plan — no Stripe or DB seeding needed.
113	- Only honored when `NODE_ENV=development`; ignored on staging/production.
114	
115	## Development
116	
117	### Available Scripts
118	
119	```bash
120	# Start everything (Supabase + Frontend)
121	npm run dev
122	
123	# Supabase management
124	npm run supabase:start    # Start Supabase
125	npm run supabase:stop     # Stop Supabase
126	npm run supabase:reset    # Reset database (migrations + seed)
127	npm run supabase:migrate  # Run migrations
128	npm run supabase:rollback # Rollback migrations by 1 step
129	npm run supabase:status   # Check Supabase status
130	
131	# Build and deploy
132	npm run build:staging     # Build for staging
133	npm run deploy:staging    # Deploy worker to Cloudflare
134	```
135	
136	### Development Workflow
137	
138	1. **First time setup:**
139	
140	   ```bash
141	   npm install
142	   cp .env.example .env.development
143	   # Edit .env.development with your values
144	   npm run dev
145	   ```
146	
147	2. **Daily development:**
148	
149	   ```bash
150	   npm run dev
151	   ```
152	
153	3. **Database changes:**
154	   ```bash
155	   # After modifying migrations
156	   npm run supabase:reset
157	   ```
158	
159	### Adding New Derivation Workers
160	
161	In order to add new derivation workers, there are a few steps to take.
162	
163	1. Add the queue to the `sync-cloud/wrangler.jsonc` file. This is done by putting it within a section titled `[[env.<env>.queues.producers]]`. Use the existing queues as an example.
164	2. Find the `queueWorkers` function within the `sync-cloud/worker/handlers.ts` file. Within, add the necessary code to queue up to your new queue.
165	3. Update the `Env` interface type within the `sync-cloud/worker/types.ts` to include your new queue binding handler.
166	4. Create your new worker folder. Add the queue to the `<your worker folder>/wrangler.jsonc` file. This is done by putting it within a section titled `[[env.<env>.queues.consumers]]`. Reference the `exchange-parser-worker/wrangler.jsonc` as an example.
167	5. **Important** In development, in order for your worker to pick up in its queue the messages that your producer sends, they have to be started as part of the same process. To do this, open `sync-cloud/vite.config.ts` and look for the `auxiliaryWorkers` section. Add your new worker as a new entry into that section. Use the `exchange-parser-worker` entry as a reference.
168	
169	You'll also want to look at the `package.json` for your new worker and add `build:staging` and `deploy:staging` (and, later, `production` variants) scripts for when it is time to build and deploy. You can also reference the `exchange-parser-worker` for that. Note as well, any `.env` files will need to be present in your new worker folder as well.
170	
171	### Architecture
172	
173	- **Frontend**: React + Vite (port 5173)
174	- **Backend**: Cloudflare Worker (proxied through Vite)
175	- **Database**: Supabase PostgreSQL (port 54321)
176	- **Authentication**: Clerk
177	- **File Storage**: Supabase Storage

```text
1	# Sessions Index (`sessions.db`)
2	
3	> **STATUS: FIRST CUT RATIFIED; LATER STAGES STRAWMAN.** The first build chunk — the
4	> `sessions.db` schema, the global-enumeration SPI method, and the `specstory reindex` command
5	> — is **agreed** and specified in
6	> [Build Plan — First Cut](#build-plan--first-cut). Everything
7	> about *keeping the index warm* (steady-state hooks, staleness, eviction) and the cloud
8	> stages remains strawman; sections still marked **OPEN** are unresolved. The reconstruction
9	> design this serves lives in [SESSION-PORTABILITY.md](SESSION-PORTABILITY.md).
10	
11	## Purpose
12	
13	`specstory resume` (cross-provider and, next, cross-project resume — see
14	[SESSION-PORTABILITY.md](SESSION-PORTABILITY.md)) needs a good selection UX: *"show me the
15	session I want to continue, wherever it came from."* For cross-project resume in
16	particular, that means surfacing sessions that originated in **other** projects, from one
17	place, with full-text search to help find them.
18	
19	Today the SPI answers only a narrower question — *"for this project dir, what sessions
20	exist?"* — by mapping a `projectPath` forward to a native store location. The resume
21	experience needs a broader, searchable view across everything we know about. `sessions.db`
22	is the proposed index that backs it.
23	
24	This doc is about **where that index lives, and WHEN entries get into it** — not the
25	column-level schema (that is deliberately deferred; see [Non-Goals](#non-goals)).
26	
27	## Decisions taken so far
28	
29	Settled in conversation:
30	
31	- **One global index, not per-project.** A single machine-level `sessions.db`
32	  (`~/.specstory/sessions.db`, no leading dot — matches its sibling `lore.db`) indexes
33	  sessions from every project, each row tagged with `project_id`. Cross-project resume's
34	  defining need is to see across projects from one place; a per-project index would force a
35	  full-disk discovery + N-database union at every pick, and a per-project index file inside
36	  `.specstory/` is either a privacy leak (if committed) or doesn't travel (if gitignored) —
37	  so it earns nothing.
38	- **Separate from `lore.db`.** Lore keeps its own corpus (`~/.specstory/lore.db`), with its
39	  own `PARSER_VERSION` cadence, fed by parsing rendered markdown. `sessions.db` is a new,
40	  independent database fed by the Go providers from raw native session data. Different
41	  inputs, different lifecycles — coupling them would couple two unrelated version cadences.
42	  They can still share discovery and the project-identity code.
43	- **Command surface: `specstory reindex` (top-level).** The full cold sweep is its own
44	  top-level command, *not* a subcommand of `resume`. The existing interactive picker stays
45	  `specstory resume`. `sessions.db` is an internal implementation-detail name — neither command
46	  is renamed to `restore`.
47	- **No new dependency.** SQLite is already vendored: `modernc.org/sqlite` (pure Go), used by
48	  the Cursor reader and `pkg/provenance/store.go`. `sessions.db` mirrors the provenance house
49	  style (`database/sql` + a `file:…?_pragma=busy_timeout=…&_pragma=journal_mode(WAL)` DSN +
50	  perf pragmas) — **not** lore's `node:sqlite` (lore is a separate Node skill; nothing shared
51	  at the code level).
52	- **First cut indexes full-body full-text, for all six providers.** `reindex` parses each
53	  session's full `SessionData` and indexes the entire conversation body into FTS5 (not a
54	  metadata-only sweep), and every provider implements the global enumerator from day one. See
55	  [Build Plan — First Cut](#build-plan--first-cut).
56	
57	## Guiding principle: `sessions.db` is a derived cache
58	
59	The authoritative source of truth is, and stays, the **native session stores**. `sessions.db`
60	is a **cache** over them. Two consequences drive the rest of this design:
61	
62	1. **It must be fully rebuildable from scratch at any time.** Deleting it is always safe.
63	2. **Incremental population is an optimization, never the only path.** If the only way data
64	   got in were live SpecStory events, any session we failed to witness would be missing
65	   *forever*. Because catchup can always rebuild, gaps are transient, not permanent.
66	
67	## Project identity: reuse the algorithm, NOT the stored files
68	
69	`pkg/utils/project_identity.go` already defines the identity *algorithm* this index needs:
70	
71	- `git_id` = `sha256(normalized origin remote URL)` → `xxxx-xxxx-xxxx-xxxx`. Derived from the
72	  remote, so it is **stable across directory, machine, and user** — the cross-project /
73	  cross-machine join key.
74	- `workspace_id` = `sha256(absolute path)` — machine-local fallback for repos with no remote.
75	
76	What is **already solved** is identity across *clones / machines*: two checkouts of the same
77	remote both compute the same `git_id` (verified — two clones of one repo, differing
78	`workspace_id`s, identical `git_id`).
79	
80	What is **NOT solved by the stored files** is the monorepo case, and this is the trap to avoid.
81	`EnsureProjectIdentity` / `generateGitID` look for `.git/config` at *exactly* the project root
82	they were given and **never walk up**. So when an agent runs from a subdirectory of a repo, the
83	written `.specstory/.project.json` there has **no `git_id`** and a fresh, path-based
84	`workspace_id` — three launch directories in one repo (`/`, `/a`, `/b`) produce three different
85	identities. **Reading the nearest stored `.project.json` would therefore *fragment* one
86	monorepo into many projects.**
87	
88	**Resolution strategy for `sessions.db` (the new part — Build Plan step 1).** Identity is
89	computed fresh per session by `ComputeProjectID(cwd)`, which **walks up from the session's cwd
90	to the git root**, computes `git_id` from *that* root's remote, and **ignores any per-directory
91	`.project.json`**. From `/a` it walks up, finds the repo's `.git`, and yields the same `git_id`
92	as `/`. Root, `/a`, `/b` all collapse to one project — which is the monorepo behavior we want.
93	It also computes `workspace_id` from the **walked-up root**, not the launch subdir, so even a
94	remote-less monorepo's subdirectories share one identity on a given machine.
95	
96	**Caveats to keep honest:**
97	
98	- **Remote-less repos** still don't cross machines: walk-up finds `.git` but no origin, so
99	  there is no `git_id`, only the path-based `workspace_id`. Subdirectories collapse (shared
100	  root), but the project is machine-local. A real constraint for the later cross-machine /
101	  cross-user stages.
102	- **No `.git` anywhere up the tree** has no natural root and genuinely fragments; that is the
103	  irreducible case.
104	
105	`project_id` (the resolved `git_id`, else `workspace_id`) is the same vocabulary the cloud sync
106	and Lore speak, so the index, the cloud, and Lore share one identity space.
107	
108	**The writer is fixed too, not just sessions.db.** To avoid maintaining two divergent identity
109	strategies, the existing `EnsureProjectIdentity` writer is switched onto the same walk-up core
110	(Build Plan step 1), so the stored `.specstory/.project.json` files stop fragmenting. The cloud
111	groups sessions by `project_id`, so monorepo-subdir sessions consequently regroup under the
112	repo's project. That is **intended and desirable**; the rare case of a previously-synced subdir
113	session "moving" cloud project is an accepted edge case, not a concern.
114	
115	## When do entries get into `sessions.db`?
116	
117	Two modes: **steady state** (warm, incremental) and **catchup** (cold, full rebuild).
118	
119	### Steady state — incremental upsert at every sighting
120	
121	The commands that already parse sessions upsert into `sessions.db` as a side effect. They
122	already hold a parsed `SessionData`, so they can populate the metadata row **and** the
123	full-text content in one shot, for free:
124	
125	- `specstory sync` — every session it processes.
126	- `specstory run` / `specstory watch` — every session update the watcher sees.
127	- `specstory resume` — a **double write**: re-index the source session, and index the
128	  freshly reconstructed target session so it is itself resumable next time.
129	
130	### The witness gap — and why more hooks don't close it
131	
132	Event-driven population only sees sessions specstory was attached to. An agent session run
133	without specstory will be absent. **This gap cannot be closed by adding more event points** —
134	there is always a session we didn't witness. The gap-closer is the catchup scan (below), run
135	opportunistically (e.g. when `reindex` finds the index stale or empty), not an ever-growing
136	list of hooks. The reframe: the gap is something the periodic scan *sweeps up*, not a hole we
137	must plug live.
138	
139	### Catchup — cold rebuild / explicit reindex
140	
141	Triggered explicitly by the user via `specstory reindex` (and, in a later chunk, automatically
142	when `sessions.db` is missing or detected stale). This is the path that enumerates *everything*
143	and is the reason for the new SPI capability below — and it is the **entirety of the first
144	cut** ([Build Plan](#build-plan--first-cut)): the only population path that exists initially.
145	
146	## The missing SPI capability: project-*discovering* enumeration
147	
148	Today's listing is project-**scoped**: `projectPath → store location → sessions`. Catchup
149	needs the inverse — enumerate **every** native session, then **discover** which project each
150	belongs to. The project becomes an *output*, not an input.
151	
152	That changes the return shape. A global enumeration must surface each session's **originating
153	cwd**, because the cwd is the only thing that lets the CLI attribute the session to a
154	`project_id`. Identity resolution stays in the CLI (one source of truth) via the new
155	read-only `ComputeProjectID(cwd)` helper (see [Build Plan](#build-plan--first-cut)) — providers
156	surface the cwd, they do not compute `project_id`.
157	
158	Signature (ratified for the first cut):
159	
160	```go
161	// ListAllAgentChatSessions enumerates every session in this provider's native store,
162	// regardless of project. Unlike ListAgentChatSessions(projectPath), the project is not an
163	// input — each returned ref carries the originating cwd so the caller can resolve project
164	// identity. Lightweight: metadata + cwd only, no full SessionData parse (reindex re-fetches
165	// full data per ref via the existing GetAgentChatSession(originCwd, sessionID)).
166	ListAllAgentChatSessions() ([]GlobalSessionRef, error)
167	
168	type GlobalSessionRef struct {
169	    SessionID  string // native session id (uuid)
170	    CreatedAt  string // ISO 8601
171	    Slug       string // human-readable, filename-safe
172	    Name       string // human-readable description (may be empty)
173	    NativePath string // absolute path to the native session file
174	    OriginCwd  string // working dir the session was launched from (→ project_id)
175	}
176	```
177	
178	**cwd is always read from *inside* the session file — uniformly, for every provider.** Claude
179	Code writes `cwd` on every JSONL record; Codex writes it in the `session_meta` record. The
180	store's *directory* is at best a hint and at worst misleading:
181	
182	- **Claude Code** — store dir is `~/.claude/projects/<cwd-encoded>/`, but the encoding
183	  (`encodeProjectDirName`) replaces *every* non-alphanumeric character with a dash and is
184	  therefore **lossy and not reversible** — do **not** try to decode cwd from the directory
185	  name; read the record `cwd`. Enumerate all project dirs, read each session's `cwd`.
186	- **Codex CLI** — sessions live under `~/.codex/sessions/YYYY/MM/DD/`, **not** project-keyed
187	  at all; cwd is inside the rollout `session_meta`. Proof that "the project is a property
188	  discovered from the session," not from its location. The existing project-scoped listing is
189	  already a global walk filtered by cwd (`findCodexSessions`) — the enumerator is that walk
190	  with the filter removed.
191	- **Gemini, Droid, DeepSeek, Cursor** — each has its own layout; same contract: return
192	  sessions + the cwd recorded inside each.
193	
194	## Monorepos: `git_id` dissolves most of it
195	
196	Because `git_id` hashes the *remote*, any cwd inside a repo boundary — child, peer, or parent
197	directory — resolves to the **same** `git_id` once we walk up to `.git` and read origin. So
198	sessions launched from different directories of one monorepo attribute to one project
199	automatically, *provided we resolve each session's cwd to its git root*.
200	
201	Sharp consequence: the cwd-scoped store lookup is **too narrow even for the current project**
202	— a session launched from a sibling directory of the same repo lives under a *different*
203	encoded store dir and a project-scoped list misses it. So "all sessions for THIS project" in a
204	monorepo is best answered by **enumerate-all-then-filter-by-`git_id`** — the same global
205	primitive — not by the forward store lookup. The new capability is therefore not only a
206	catchup tool; it is also the correct primitive for the monorepo current-project view.
207	
208	Still fragments: remote-less directories (only `workspace_id`, which is path-based). Flagged,
209	not solved.
210	
211	## Two fill-levels (a future optimization, not the first cut)
212	
213	The index has two natural fill-levels:
214	
215	1. **Existence + metadata** — `project_id`, `uuid`, `agent`, `date`, `slug`, native path.
216	   Obtainable cheaply from the global enumeration (no `SessionData` parse). Enough to *browse
217	   and pick*.
218	2. **Content / full-text** — requires parsing `SessionData`.
219	
220	**First-cut decision: `reindex` does both at once — it parses full `SessionData` and indexes
221	the whole conversation body into FTS5.** A *first* index of a session is therefore a full
222	parse, not a cheap metadata sweep; full-body search is the UX we want from day one.
223	
224	**`reindex` is incremental, though.** It loads every indexed session's freshness fingerprint
225	(`size + mtime + index_version`) up front and **skips any session whose native file is
226	unchanged and was indexed by the current logic version** — exactly Lore's idempotency contract.
227	So the *first* run is a full parse, but re-runs only touch new/changed sessions (verified:
228	~20s → ~2s with most sessions unchanged). `--force` re-indexes everything; bumping
229	`index_version` (when parse/derivation logic changes) auto-invalidates every row. The cheap
230	metadata-only enumeration still runs every time (it's how sessions are discovered), but the
231	expensive full parse is gated by the fingerprint.
232	
233	The two-level split also keeps the index warm *without* an explicit `reindex`, two ways:
234	
235	- **`resume`/`search` background warm.** While the picker is open, a background goroutine
236	  (`warmIndexInBackground`) runs the same incremental engine over its own writer handle in two
237	  silent passes — the **current project first** (so its rows refresh almost immediately, and the
238	  open TUI re-queries via `indexWarmedMsg`), then the **full corpus**. It reuses the exact
239	  `enumerateAll` → `dedupRefs` → `selectWork` → `processWork` engine the foreground `reindex`
240	  uses (only the progress reporter differs: live bars vs. a silent `nopReporter`). It is
241	  cancelled the instant the TUI exits and never blocks process exit — an abandoned write batch
242	  is safe under WAL. It is skipped when the index was just built fresh in the foreground (see
243	  `openOrBuildResumeIndex` → `builtFresh`).
244	
245	- **Real-time upserts from `watch`/`run`/`resume`-launch.** These already write a markdown file
246	  on every detected session change; a `LiveIndexer` (held for the command's lifetime) mirrors
247	  each change into the index with a single-row `Upsert`, reusing the same content derivation
248	  (`flattenBody`/`countTurns`/`lastTimestamp`). The project is resolved once (a watch/run has a
249	  fixed cwd); repeat callbacks with no new activity are skipped. A live row carries **no
250	  native-file fingerprint** (Size/Mtime/NativePath are unknown without enumerating), so the next
251	  `reindex`/warm re-verifies and rewrites it with a stable fingerprint — the live row is correct
252	  and queryable in the interim. All of it is best-effort: indexing never disrupts the agent or
253	  the markdown write (a nil `LiveIndexer` is a safe no-op; per-update errors log at debug).
254	
255	- **`sync` indexes as it goes.** `sync`/`sync <provider>`/`sync -s` already load every session's
256	  full `SessionData` for the current project, so each is `Record`ed into the index via the same
257	  `LiveIndexer` — indexing is essentially free there. `--print` (stdout, no save) is excluded.
258	
259	## Build Plan — First Cut
260	
261	Scope: the cold-rebuild path only — `reindex` + the global enumerator + the schema. The
262	interactive picker's *rewiring* to read `sessions.db`, and all warm-keeping, are later chunks.
263	
264	1. **Shared walk-up identity core** — extract one resolver in
265	   `pkg/utils/project_identity.go` that, given a directory, walks **up** to the git root
266	   (nearest ancestor with `.git`, handling `.git` as a **file** for worktrees/submodules, not
267	   just a directory); computes `git_id` from *that root's* remote (reusing `normalizeGitURL` /
268	   `createHash`), else `workspace_id` from the **same walked-up root** (so remote-less monorepo
269	   subdirs still collapse to one id). Two callers share it:
270	   - `ComputeProjectID(cwd) (id, name, err)` — **read-only**, used by `reindex`. Ignores any
271	     per-directory `.specstory/.project.json` (those fragment a monorepo) and never writes one.
272	   - `EnsureProjectIdentity` — the existing **writer**, switched onto the same core so the
273	     stored files stop fragmenting. Existing subdir files self-correct (they get the repo
274	     `git_id` + name on next run). This regroups monorepo-subdir sessions under the repo's
275	     cloud project — **intended** (the cloud groups sessions by `project_id`); the rare
276	     prior-synced subdir sessions "moving" cloud project is acceptable. See
277	     [Project identity](#project-identity-reuse-the-algorithm-not-the-stored-files).
278	
279	2. **SPI extension** — add `GlobalSessionRef` + `ListAllAgentChatSessions()` to the
280	   `spi.Provider` interface (type in a small new `pkg/spi/global.go`). Lightweight; cwd read
281	   from inside each session file.
282	
283	3. **Per-provider enumerators — all six.** Mostly "existing store walk, minus the project
284	   filter, plus surface the recorded cwd." Cursor (SQLite `store.db`) gets the most care.
285	
286	4. **New store package `pkg/sessionindex`** — `sessions.db` in the provenance house style
287	   (`database/sql` + `modernc.org/sqlite`, WAL DSN + perf pragmas). Two tables (full column
288	   specs in [Schema](#schema)). FTS body = the reconstruction-flatten of `SessionData` (plain
289	   user/agent turns, synthetic noise already stripped — provider-neutral, reuses existing
290	   code). API: `Open`, `Upsert`, `Search`, lazy `Snippets`, `ListByProject`, and project
291	   rollups.
292	
293	5. **`specstory reindex` command** — a new top-level command (its own `pkg/cmd/reindex.go`,
294	   registered in `main.go` alongside `resume`). Enumerated refs are first **deduped by
295	   `(agent, session_id)`, keeping the freshest file by mtime** — a resumed session can span
296	   multiple native files sharing one id, and they all map to one row, so without dedup the
297	   duplicates ping-pong (each run, one file's stat never matches the fingerprint the other just
298	   stored, re-indexing both forever). Then per deduped session: stat the native file → skip if
299	   its `size + mtime + index_version` fingerprint is unchanged (the incremental path; `--force`
300	   overrides) → else `ComputeProjectID(OriginCwd)` → `GetAgentChatSession(OriginCwd, SessionID)`
301	   for full data → flatten body + count turns + derive timestamps → `Upsert` (metadata + FTS,
302	   `INSERT OR REPLACE`). Runs as a concurrent pipeline — see
303	   [Reindex Concurrency Model](#reindex-concurrency-model). Refs with no resolvable cwd (a few
304	   Claude warmups; all Cursor for now) are indexed metadata-only under the `unknown` project_id
305	   rather than dropped; refs with no native id are skipped (unresumable, and would collide on
306	   the primary key). Dedup also makes the "found" count equal the indexed count.
307	
308	6. **Tests** — table-driven: identity walk-up (subdir / monorepo / no-remote), store
309	   upsert+FTS round-trip, per-provider enumeration against fixtures.
310	
311	### Reindex Concurrency Model
312	
313	The hot path is the per-session full parse (`GetAgentChatSession` → `SessionData` → flatten
314	body, count turns, derive timestamps). Each session is an independent, read-only parse of its
315	own native file — embarrassingly parallel. `reindex` runs a **3-stage streaming pipeline**:
316	
317	```
318	enumerate (6 providers, parallel)  →  parse+build (bounded worker pool)  →  write (1 goroutine)
319	      cheap, independent                  the hot CPU+IO fan-out             SQLite single-writer
320	```
321	
322	- **Enumerate** — the six `ListAllAgentChatSessions()` run concurrently; each walks its own
323	  store. Cheap, and lets parsing start streaming before enumeration finishes.
324	- **Parse + build** — a bounded worker pool (`min(NumCPU, ~8–12)`) over all refs. Workers are
325	  pure `ref → sessionindex.Session`. A per-session parse failure is logged and skipped, never aborts
326	  the sweep.
327	- **Write** — a *single* writer goroutine drains a channel and upserts in **batched
328	  transactions** (commit every ~200 rows). SQLite is single-writer (`MaxOpenConns=1`), so this
329	  serializes anyway; batching avoids thousands of tiny WAL commits — the main perf lever after
330	  parse concurrency.
331	
332	**Streaming, not collect-then-write:** session bodies are large (1–5 MB each), so parsed
333	sessions stream parse → FTS-index → discard; we never retain a body after its upsert, keeping
334	memory bounded.
335	
336	**`cwd → project_id` cache.** Many sessions share a cwd (same project), and `ComputeProjectID`
337	walks the filesystem to the git root each call. A mutex-guarded `map[cwd]projectID` (or a
338	pre-pass over the unique cwd set) eliminates the redundant walks.
339	
340	**Provider concurrency-safety** is a precondition: `GetAgentChatSession` is called from N
341	goroutines, so the providers' parse paths must hold no shared mutable state. Audited before
342	implementation (providers are effectively stateless; per-call caches like Cursor's
343	`MessageTimestampCache` are local).
344	
345	**No cross-provider barrier in this cut.** The deferred Cursor cwd recovery (above) *will*
346	introduce one (collect all other cwds before md5-matching Cursor); until then the pipeline is
347	fully streaming.
348	
349	### Reindex Progress UX
350	
351	`reindex` aims for a world-class, engaging readout. All progress goes to **stderr** (stdout
352	reserved for a future `--emit json`); the renderer is **TTY-aware**. Three moments:
353	
354	1. **Discover** (instant — enumeration is fast and runs first):
355	
356	   ```
357	   🔍  Scanning 6 agents…
358	   ✓   Found 822 sessions  ·  claude 683 · codex 70 · cursor 49 · droid 16 · deepseek 3 · gemini 1
359	   ```
360	
361	2. **Index** (the long parse phase) — a **multi-line, in-place per-agent progress block**, one
362	   bar per agent ticking independently, plus an aggregate header:
363	
364	   ```
365	   Indexing  512/822 · 23 projects · 130/s
366	
367	     claude   ▕███████████░░░▏ 470/683
368	     codex    ▕██████████████▏  70/70 ✓
369	     cursor   ▕████░░░░░░░░░░▏  12/49
370	     droid    ▕██████████████▏  16/16 ✓
371	     deepseek ▕██████████████▏   3/3  ✓
372	     gemini   ▕██████████████▏   1/1  ✓
373	   ```
374	
375	   Implementation: workers bump **atomic per-agent counters**; a single render goroutine ticks
376	   (~10 Hz) and redraws the block in place via ANSI cursor-up. The distinct-project counter is a
377	   mutex-guarded set. No worker draws directly (avoids interleaving). Fixed-width bars; no color
378	   dependency.
379	
380	3. **Summary** — a clean, scannable final block, honest about gaps:
381	
382	   ```
383	   ✓   Indexed 822 sessions into ~/.specstory/sessions.db  (6.1s)
384	
385	         claude 683   codex 70   cursor 49   droid 16   deepseek 3   gemini 1
386	
387	         31 projects  ·  49 unattributed
388	   ```
389	
390	**Non-TTY fallback** (piped / CI): no ANSI, no spinner — periodic plain `indexed N/822…` lines
391	plus the same final summary, so logs stay clean.
392	
393	## Schema
394	
395	`~/.specstory/sessions.db`. Two tables.
396	
397	### `sessions` — one row per known session
398	
399	| Column          | Type    | Description                                                                                                                                            |
400	|-----------------|---------|--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
401	| `project_id`    | TEXT    | Resolved identity (walk-up `git_id`, else `workspace_id`). The value the cloud groups by and Lore speaks. Indexed.                                     |
402	| `project_name`  | TEXT    | Human-readable project name (repo name from the walked-up root).                                                                                       |
403	| `agent`         | TEXT    | Provider id: `claude`, `codex`, `gemini`, `droid`, `deepseek`, `cursor`. Part of the primary key.                                                      |
404	| `session_id`    | TEXT    | Native session id (uuid). Part of the primary key.                                                                                                     |
405	| `created_at`    | TEXT    | ISO 8601 session creation timestamp (first turn). Powers the "Created" sort.                                                                           |
406	| `updated_at`    | TEXT    | ISO 8601 last-activity timestamp (last turn, else file mtime). Powers "X ago", the "Updated" sort, and resume-last.                                    |
407	| `user_turns`    | INTEGER | Count of user prompts — the headline "how much work is here" signal.                                                                                   |
408	| `total_turns`   | INTEGER | Count of all messages (user + agent). Computed alongside `user_turns`.                                                                                 |
409	| `slug`          | TEXT    | Filename-safe slug derived from the first user message.                                                                                                |
410	| `name`          | TEXT    | Human-readable session description (may be empty).                                                                                                     |
411	| `native_path`   | TEXT    | Absolute path the provider opens to read this session — a JSONL/JSON file for most agents, or a per-session `store.db` for Cursor. Unique per session. |
412	| `origin_cwd`    | TEXT    | Working directory the session was launched from (the input to identity resolution).                                                                    |
413	| `size`          | INTEGER | Native file size in bytes — part of the freshness fingerprint (incremental-skip on re-run).                                                            |
414	| `mtime`         | INTEGER | Native file modification time, epoch ms — part of the freshness fingerprint.                                                                           |
415	| `index_version` | INTEGER | reindex logic version that wrote the row — part of the fingerprint; bumping it forces a full re-parse.                                                 |
416	| `indexed_at`    | TEXT    | ISO 8601 time this row was last written by `reindex`.                                                                                                  |
417	| `fts_rowid`     | INTEGER | rowid of this session's `sessions_fts` row — the O(1) link used to read the body and to delete-before-insert without scanning the FTS (see below). NULL on rows written before this column existed, until a `reindex` repopulates them. |
418	
419	Primary key: `(agent, session_id)` — a session is unique within a provider, and belongs to
420	exactly one project. `project_id` is indexed for per-project filtering. `created_at` /
421	`updated_at` / `user_turns` / `total_turns` come from the full `SessionData` parse `reindex`
422	already performs; the rest come from the lightweight enumeration ref.
423	
424	**Considered and deliberately excluded (first cut):**
425	
426	- **Git branch.** Claude Code records `gitBranch` per turn (stable within a session), but Codex
427	  and the others record nothing — a half-populated, Claude-only column isn't worth it yet. If
428	  added later it belongs on the enumeration ref as native metadata, *not* in neutral
429	  `SessionData`.
430	- **User naming / rename.** No `custom_name`; sessions are not renameable in the first cut.
431	  Keeps `sessions` a purely rebuildable cache (no user-authoritative fields to preserve across
432	  `reindex`).
433	- **Lineage.** No `source_session_id`. The breadcrumb already exists natively for free —
434	  reconstruction writes `specstorySourceSessionId` (the source session id) into the rebuilt
435	  file's meta (`claudecode`/`codexcli`/`droidcli` `reconstruct.go`) — so it can be surfaced
436	  later (ideally also capturing the source *agent*, which that field does not) when fork/resume
437	  lineage UX is actually designed.
438	
439	### `sessions_fts` — FTS5 full-text index (kept in tandem with `sessions`)
440	
441	| Column       | In FTS index?    | Description                                                                                     |
442	|--------------|------------------|-------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
443	| `session_id` | No (`UNINDEXED`) | Join key back to `sessions`; stored in the row but not tokenized.                               |
444	| `agent`      | No (`UNINDEXED`) | Join key back to `sessions`; stored in the row but not tokenized.                               |
445	| `name`       | Yes              | Session description / first-message-derived name; tokenized + searchable.                       |
446	| `body`       | Yes              | Full conversation text — the reconstruction-flattened user/agent turns; tokenized + searchable. |
447	
448	`UNINDEXED` is an FTS5 per-column keyword meaning the column is **stored but excluded from the
449	full-text index** — not "lacks a b-tree index" (FTS5 tables have no secondary b-tree indexes at
450	all). The two join keys ride along in the row so a `MATCH` hit maps straight back to its
451	`sessions` row without a separate lookup table. Default FTS5 tokenizer. Rows are
452	inserted/replaced alongside their `sessions` row during
453	`reindex`; deletion of a `sessions` row removes its `sessions_fts` row.
454	
455	**Reaching a *specific* FTS row is by `fts_rowid`, never by the join keys.** Because
456	`session_id`/`agent` are `UNINDEXED`, a point query like `WHERE agent=? AND session_id=?`
457	against `sessions_fts` has nothing to seek on and **scans the entire table** — fine for a
458	`MATCH` search (which uses the full-text index), O(N) for a single-row lookup. So the writer
459	stores each FTS row's rowid on its `sessions` row (`fts_rowid`) at insert time
460	(`last_insert_rowid()`), and:
461	
462	- **Body reads** (`SessionBody`, the preview pane) join `sessions_fts ON rowid = sessions.fts_rowid`,
463	  an O(1) rowid lookup, with a one-time fallback to the by-key scan for rows whose `fts_rowid`
464	  is still NULL (written before the column existed; a `reindex` retires the fallback).
465	- **Replace-before-insert** deletes the prior FTS row by `WHERE rowid = ?` rather than by the
466	  UNINDEXED keys. Brand-new sessions skip the lookup+delete entirely (`Session.IsNew`), since
467	  there is no prior row.
468	
469	This is why the body lookup and the per-row delete stay O(1) as the index grows into the tens of
470	thousands of rows, instead of each becoming a full-table scan.
471	
472	## Non-Goals (first cut)
473	
474	- **The picker rewiring.** `specstory resume`'s interactive flow still uses the project-scoped
475	  `ListAgentChatSessions` until a later chunk points it at `sessions.db`.
476	- **Storing serialized `SessionData`.** The first cut stores metadata + full-text body, not a
477	  `SessionData` blob. A blob becomes relevant for cloud Stages 3–4 (where the cloud is the
478	  source). Deferred.
479	
480	## Deferred — DO NEXT (Cursor cwd recovery)
481	
482	Cursor CLI sessions are currently enumerated with `OriginCwd=""` and therefore indexed
483	under the **`unknown` project_id**. This is a first-cut shortcut, not the end state — it is
484	the immediate follow-up after the `reindex` first cut.
485	
486	Cursor stores sessions at `~/.cursor/chats/<projectHash>/<sessionID>/store.db`, where
487	`projectHash = md5(canonical project path)` (`cursorcli/path_utils.go` `GetProjectHashDir`),
488	and records no workspace path inside the store. md5 is one-way, but the hash is embedded in
489	`GlobalSessionRef.NativePath` (two directories up from `store.db`). **Recovery plan:** the
490	`reindex` orchestrator builds `map[md5(canonicalize(cwd))]cwd` from every *other* provider's
491	cwds (optionally augmented by a filesystem scan for git/`.specstory` roots), then matches each
492	Cursor ref's `projectHash` to recover its cwd → resolve `project_id` via `ComputeProjectID`.

## Summary: Understanding "Workspace" in specstory-sync

## 1. **Database Schema Definition**

**File:** `/Users/jakelevirne/dev/specstory-sync/supabase/schema.sql` (lines 5-12)

```sql
CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS workspaces (
  id UUID DEFAULT gen_random_uuid() PRIMARY KEY,
  project_id TEXT NOT NULL,
  owner_id TEXT NOT NULL,
  name TEXT NOT NULL,
  created_at TIMESTAMP WITH TIME ZONE DEFAULT NOW(),
  updated_at TIMESTAMP WITH TIME ZONE DEFAULT NOW()
);
```

**Extended Columns** (added later via migrations):
- `icon` TEXT (line 227 in `/Users/jakelevirne/dev/specstory-sync/shared/db/schema.ts`)
- `color` TEXT (line 228 in shared/db/schema.ts)

**Primary Keys & Unique Constraints:**
- Primary key: `id` (UUID auto-generated)
- Unique constraint: `(project_id, owner_id)` — exactly one workspace per user per project (line 51 in schema.sql)

### `workspace_sessions_summary` View
**File:** `/Users/jakelevirne/dev/specstory-sync/supabase/schema.sql` (lines 221-236)

```sql
CREATE OR REPLACE VIEW workspace_sessions_summary AS
SELECT 
  w.id,
  w.project_id,
  w.owner_id,
  w.name,
  w.icon,
  w.color,
  w.created_at,
  w.updated_at,
  COUNT(s.id) as session_count,
  MAX(s.updated_at) as last_session,
  COALESCE(SUM(s.markdown_size), 0) as total_markdown_size
FROM workspaces w
LEFT JOIN sessions s ON w.id = s.workspace_id
GROUP BY w.id, w.project_id, w.owner_id, w.name, w.icon, w.color, w.created_at, w.updated_at;
```

This view aggregates workspace metadata with session statistics (count, last update timestamp, total size).

```typescript
export interface CreateWorkspaceData {
  projectId: string; // String workspace ID
  name: string;
  userId: string;
  icon?: string;
  color?: string;
}

export async function upsertWorkspace(
  data: CreateWorkspaceData
): Promise<Workspace> {
  // Check if workspace already exists
  const { data: existingWorkspace } = await supabaseClient()
    .from("workspaces")
    .select("id, icon, color")
    .eq("project_id", data.projectId)
    .eq("owner_id", data.userId)
    .maybeSingle();

  // Upsert (insert or update) the workspace
  const { data: workspace, error } = await supabaseClient()
    .from("workspaces")
    .upsert(
      {
        project_id: data.projectId,
        owner_id: data.userId,
        name: data.name,
        icon: defaultIcon,
        color: defaultColor,
      },
      {
        onConflict: "project_id,owner_id",  // Key uniqueness
      }
    )
    .select()
    .maybeSingle();

  // Create user permission
  if (data.userId) {
    await createUserPermission(
      data.userId,
      workspace.id as string,
      data.projectId
    );
  }
  // ...
}
```

### Schema Analysis Doc
**File:** `/Users/jakelevirne/dev/specstory-sync/docs/supabase-schema-usage-analysis.md` (lines 29-34, 55)

```
SpecStory Cloud stores synced AI coding history as:

workspaces
  -> sessions
    -> exchanges
      -> exchange_chunks
        -> chunk_embeddings

workspaces: one cloud-side project workspace for a user and client project id. 
Current code creates/upserts by (project_id, owner_id).
```

## **Semantic Summary**

A **workspace** in SpecStory is:

1. **A user-scoped project container** — one workspace per (Clerk user ID, client project ID) pair.
2. **Identified by two keys:**
   - **Internal UUID** (`id`): Cloud-generated, used for foreign key relationships
   - **Client identifier** (`project_id`): Client-generated string (typically a local project/repo path or name)
   - **Owner** (`owner_id`): Clerk user ID of the workspace creator/owner

3. **Contains sessions** — each workspace holds multiple AI chat sessions, all synced from the same local project.

4. **Supports access control** — the `user_permissions` table allows the owner to grant other Clerk users read/write access to a workspace via the same `(workspace_id, project_id)` pair.

5. **Tracks metadata** — name, icon (emoji/glyph), color (for UI), plus aggregated statistics (session count, last activity, total markdown size) computed by the `workspace_sessions_summary` view.

6. **Cascades on deletion** — removing a workspace cascade-deletes all its sessions, exchanges, chunks, and embeddings.

## Summary

I've thoroughly explored the specstory-cli codebase to understand how it identifies and syncs histories to a remote sync service. Here are my findings:

### **1. PROJECT IDENTIFICATION & GROUPING**

The CLI uses a **project identity system** stored in `.specstory/.project.json` that contains:

**File: `/Users/jakelevirne/dev/getspecstory/specstory-cli/pkg/cloud/sync.go` (lines 98-102)**
```go
type ProjectData struct {
    ProjectName string `json:"project_name"`
    GitID       string `json:"git_id"`
    WorkspaceID string `json:"workspace_id"`
}
```

**Actual example from this repo** (`.specstory/.project.json`):
```json
{
  "workspace_id": "cdac-49ff-91e4-e62f",
  "workspace_id_at": "2026-06-17T21:41:30Z",
  "git_id": "0f81-fa3b-cc40-b565",
  "git_id_at": "2026-06-17T21:41:30Z",
  "project_name": "getspecstory"
}
```

**Key points:**
- All history/sessions in the same project are grouped and synced together as a unit
- A **project** in specstory-cli terminology corresponds to what the sync service calls a "workspace"
- The project is identified by a **`projectId`** that is sent to the cloud API (see below)

### **2. PROJECT ID RESOLUTION (Critical for sync)**

**File: `/Users/jakelevirne/dev/getspecstory/specstory-cli/pkg/cloud/sync.go` (lines 746-759)**
```go
// Determine project ID - use git_id if present, otherwise workspace_id
projectID := ""
if projectData != nil && projectData.GitID != "" {
    projectID = projectData.GitID
} else if projectData != nil && projectData.WorkspaceID != "" {
    projectID = projectData.WorkspaceID
}

// Project ID is required for cloud sync
if projectID == "" {
    slog.Warn("Cannot sync session to cloud: no project ID available", "sessionId", sessionID)
    syncMgr.stats.trackSessionInCategory(sessionID, categoryErrored)
    return
}
```

**Resolution hierarchy:**
1. **`git_id`** — Hash of the normalized git origin remote URL (preferred, travels across machines/users/clones)
2. **`workspace_id`** — Hash of the absolute filesystem path (fallback when no git remote)

Both are 16-character hex strings formatted as `xxxx-xxxx-xxxx-xxxx`.

### **3. PAYLOAD SENT TO SYNC API**

**File: `/Users/jakelevirne/dev/getspecstory/specstory-cli/pkg/cloud/sync.go` (lines 79-87, 793-821)**

```go
type APIRequest struct {
    ProjectID   string             `json:"projectId"`      // The resolved project ID (git_id or workspace_id)
    ProjectName string             `json:"projectName"`    // Human-readable name (repo name or directory)
    Name        string             `json:"name"`           // Session name
    Markdown    string             `json:"markdown"`       // Full markdown content
    RawData     string             `json:"rawData"`        // Raw JSONL session data

_**Agent (claude-opus-4-8 2026-07-01 15:17:39Z)**_

Both explorations are in, and they line up cleanly. Here's the answer.

## What a "workspace" is in specstory-sync

A **workspace is a per-user project container** — one row per `(project_id, owner_id)` pair. It's the top of the cloud data hierarchy:

```
workspace → sessions → exchanges → chunks → embeddings
```

The [`workspaces`](../specstory-sync/supabase/schema.sql) table:

```sql
id          UUID    -- cloud-generated primary key
project_id  TEXT    -- client-generated identifier (the join key to the CLI)
owner_id    TEXT    -- Clerk user id
name        TEXT
icon, color TEXT
```

- **Unique constraint** on `(project_id, owner_id)` → exactly one workspace per user per project.
- `sessions.workspace_id` and `user_permissions.workspace_id` both FK into it (cascade delete).
- The [`workspace_sessions_summary`](../specstory-sync/supabase/schema.sql) view just decorates each workspace with aggregates: `COUNT(sessions)`, `MAX(updated_at)`, `SUM(markdown_size)`. It's the "workspace + stats" read model for the UI, nothing more.

## The CLI concept it maps to

Yes — your intuition is right. A **workspace in the cloud == a "project" in the CLI**. The bridge is one field: `workspaces.project_id` is exactly the `projectId` the CLI sends.

On the CLI side, the identity lives in [`.specstory/.project.json`](specstory-cli/pkg/utils/project_identity.go) and is resolved in [sync.go:746](specstory-cli/pkg/cloud/sync.go#L746):

```go
// prefer git_id, fall back to workspace_id
projectID := projectData.GitID
if projectID == "" { projectID = projectData.WorkspaceID }
```

Two possible identifiers, both a 16-char hash formatted `xxxx-xxxx-xxxx-xxxx`:

| CLI field | Derived from | Property |
|-----------|-------------|----------|
| `git_id` | hash of normalized git origin remote URL | **preferred** — stable across clones/machines/users |
| `workspace_id` | hash of the canonical absolute directory path | fallback when there's no git remote — local to that machine |

The CLI PUTs each session to `/api/v1/projects/{projectId}/sessions/{sessionId}` with `projectId` + `projectName`. The cloud worker's [`upsertWorkspace()`](../specstory-sync/sync-cloud/worker/handlers/sessions.ts#L58) then does:

```ts
upsertWorkspace({ projectId, name: projectName, userId })
// onConflict: "project_id,owner_id"
```

So the workspace is **created lazily on first session sync** — the CLI never explicitly "creates a workspace." It just syncs sessions tagged with a `projectId`, and the cloud upserts a workspace to hold them.

## The one naming trap

The word "workspace" means **different things** on each side — don't let it mislead you:

- **CLI `workspace_id`** = the path-based fallback identifier (one of two candidates for `projectId`).
- **Cloud `workspace`** = the whole project container, whose `project_id` is usually the CLI's **`git_id`**, not the CLI's `workspace_id`.

So a cloud workspace is the CLI's notion of a **project**, and it's most often keyed by the CLI's `git_id`. The CLI's `workspace_id` only becomes the cloud `project_id` when the repo has no git remote.

**Net:** cloud `workspaces.project_id` ← CLI resolved `projectId` (`git_id` ?? `workspace_id`), scoped per Clerk user via `owner_id`. That composite is what makes "my copy of this repo's history" one distinct workspace.

_**Agent (claude-opus-4-8 2026-07-01 15:33:48Z)**_

Good — this is exactly the right thing to nail down before touching schema. Let me lay out a point of view, then run your questions through it.

## The core reframe

Your "easy YES" is actually the load-bearing question, because **today the answer is NO.** Right now a workspace is keyed `(project_id, owner_id=user)`. Two teammates on the same repo resolve the same `git_id` but different `owner_id`, so they get **two separate workspaces**. Nothing about adding an org table changes that by itself.

So the whole point of the org model is to move the axis of ownership. The Vercel lesson that matters most here:

> **A project belongs to a *scope* (a team, or a personal account), not to a user. Git is an *attribute* of the project, not its identity.**

Everything else follows from porting those two ideas.

## Five principles (Vercel → SpecStory)

1. **Ownership is a scope, and a personal account is just a scope with one member.** Replace `owner_id: user` with an owner that is *either* a user's personal scope *or* an org. Uniqueness becomes `(git_id, owner_scope)`. This is Vercel's Hobby-account-vs-Team duality applied verbatim.

2. **The git repo is a rebindable attribute, not identity.** The workspace's identity is its own UUID. `git_id` / `workspace_id` are *aliases* that route sessions to it — and a workspace can gain, lose, or swap aliases over its life without losing history. (This is what makes Q4 tractable.)

3. **Same repo → N independent workspaces across scopes is normal, not a conflict.** `git_id` is unique *within* a scope, never globally. Alice-personal, Org A, and Org B can all have a workspace for repo R simultaneously. No cross-talk.

4. **Membership grants access; leaving revokes it; the resource stays with the scope.** You never "take the team's workspace with you" when you leave.

5. **Merging/moving between scopes is always an explicit act, never a side effect** of joining or leaving.

There's one new piece these force into existence, which I'll flag as the real open decision: **the CLI must resolve not just *which project* but *which scope* to sync into** — the direct analog of Vercel's `.vercel/project.json { orgId, projectId }`. I'd add a scope/`org_id` field to `.specstory/.project.json` next to `git_id`. Default = personal; binding to an org is deliberate.

## Your questions, answered from this POV

| Scenario | Answer |
|---|---|
| **Same org, same repo, both sync** | **One workspace** — *if* both are bound to the org scope. Upsert key `(git_id, org)` collapses them. The moving part isn't the repo match (that already works), it's that both CLIs must be syncing into the org scope, not their personal scopes. |
| **Not same org → both join org O** | **Nothing automatic.** Their two personal workspaces stay personal and private. Joining a team never migrates personal projects (Vercel doesn't either). To collaborate, someone must *explicitly bring the repo into org O.* |
| **…and when they bring it into O** | They converge on the single `(git_id, O)` workspace. Because sessions carry **author provenance**, this is a lossless *merge*: both people's sessions re-parent into the one org workspace, each still attributed to its author/device/agent. No "who wins" — it's additive at the session level. |
| **One of them leaves O** | Everything synced into O's workspace **stays with O.** The leaver loses cloud access. They lose *nothing real*, because their local `.specstory/history/` is the source of truth they always retain — they lost the shared cloud copy, not their work. (If they were the last member/owner → normal org-lifecycle: transfer or delete-cascade.) |
| **Two orgs, separate workspaces, same repo** | **Fully independent and expected.** `(git_id, A)` and `(git_id, B)` are different workspaces with their own members, sessions, access. This is the direct Vercel analog and the right call — `git_id` is not globally unique. |
| **Non-git folder → becomes a GitHub repo** | The workspace should **keep its identity and gain the `git_id` as a new alias** — *not* spawn a fresh workspace. Today the resolved `project_id` flips from `workspace_id` (path hash) to `git_id` (remote hash); naive upsert would orphan the pre-git history. The fix: the workspace's durable ID is its UUID, and the CLI — which already stores *both* ids with timestamps in `.project.json` — signals "attach `git_id G` to the workspace previously keyed by `workspace_id W`." History carries forward, and the repo becoming a repo is also the moment it becomes *shareable* (teammates cloning it now resolve G and land in the same workspace). |

## What this implies for the schema (when you do build it)

Three changes fall out, and they're the ones worth designing carefully:

1. **Owner becomes a scope.** Either an `organizations` table + nullable `workspaces.org_id` (null = personal, owned by `owner_id`), or a polymorphic `(owner_type, owner_id)`. Uniqueness moves to `(git_id, scope)`. Access for org workspaces is **derived from org membership**, so `user_permissions` evolves from "the sharing table" into "memberships + personal-workspace shares."

2. **Sessions get author provenance.** Add `authored_by` (Clerk user) / `device_id` / `agent_name` at the *session* level (some is already in the CLI's metadata payload). Without this, merges and departures are lossy and unattributable. This is the single most important enabling change — it's what makes "merge two workspaces" and "who contributed what after someone leaves" answerable.

3. **`project_id` becomes a rebindable alias set, not the identity.** Support attaching a `git_id` to an existing workspace, and a "rebind/migrate" operation the CLI triggers on the git transition. Longer term, note a limitation worth writing down now: identity-by-remote-URL-hash can't survive a GitHub rename/transfer/fork (the URL changes → new `git_id`). If that matters, the more robust key is GitHub's immutable repo node id when available — same alias machinery, sturdier alias.

## The one decision that's genuinely yours

**Where do sessions go by default, and how does the CLI choose scope?**

My recommendation, straight from Vercel: **default to the personal scope**, and make binding-a-project-to-an-org an explicit act (interactive link, or a rule like "you're a member of O and a teammate already has this repo in O — link it?"). Rationale: it's the privacy-safe default — you never accidentally publish your AI history into an org — and it keeps the frictionless desktop-sync behavior intact while making collaboration opt-in. The tension to resolve is that Vercel's linking is deliberate (`vercel link`) whereas your desktop sync is meant to be automatic; auto-grouping *within* a scope is fine, but *choosing the org scope* is where I'd keep a human in the loop.

_**Agent (claude-opus-4-8 2026-07-01 15:36:42Z)**_

Right — Vercel supports git-less projects, and looking at *how* it does exposes a flaw in the way I stated the key. Let me correct it.

## Why `workspace_id` can't play git's role

`git_id` and `workspace_id` are not two flavors of the same thing. They differ on the one property that matters for a uniqueness key across a scope: **shareability.**

- **`git_id`** = hash of the normalized remote URL. It *intentionally collides* across users and machines — Alice's clone and Bob's clone produce the same hash. That collision is the whole mechanism that lets "same repo → same workspace" happen automatically.
- **`workspace_id`** = hash of the canonical absolute path. It *never* meaningfully collides. `/Users/alice/dev/foo` and `/Users/bob/work/foo` are different hashes even when it's conceptually "the same project." It's a per-machine, per-path local fingerprint.

So `(workspace_id, scope)` as a uniqueness key only ever matches *you, on this machine, at this path.* It can't group a non-git project across two people, or even across your own two laptops. Putting a path-hash workspace into an org scope doesn't make it joinable — no teammate will ever resolve that same hash.

## How Vercel actually handles it — and the fix

A git-less Vercel project has identity anyway: a **server-assigned project ID**. Other machines/members don't *derive* it, they **link** to it — `.vercel/project.json` stores `{ orgId, projectId }`, and every `vercel deploy` from any linked checkout targets that same server ID. Grouping is by explicit link, not by content collision.

Port that directly. The general uniqueness key isn't `(git_id, scope)` — it's **`(binding, scope)`**, where a binding is one of two kinds:

| Binding | Derived from | Collides across users? | Role |
|---|---|---|---|
| **Portable** (`git_id`, later maybe GitHub node id) | shared remote | Yes, by design | Enables *automatic* grouping |
| **Explicit link** (workspace UUID) | server-assigned, stored in `.project.json` | Yes, because everyone stores the same UUID | Enables grouping when there's nothing to derive |
| **Local** (`workspace_id` path hash) | absolute path | No | Only a *default* to keep one machine's sessions together |

Auto-collapse (`upsert onConflict`) happens **only on portable bindings**. For a git-less project you want to share, you fall back to exactly Vercel's move: the workspace has its durable **server UUID**, and each contributor joins it by writing that UUID into their local `.specstory/.project.json` — the direct analog of `.vercel/project.json { projectId }`. The path-hash `workspace_id` gets demoted to "local default grouping only," never a sharing key.

## The payoff

This also makes the "folder becomes a repo" transition fall out for free. A git-less project **already has its UUID identity** and its contributors already attached (by explicit link or their own path hash). When git arrives, `git_id` simply becomes a *new portable binding* on that same workspace — nothing re-parents, and now *new* teammates can auto-join by derivation instead of explicit link. Identity was never the git id; the git id was always just the most convenient binding when it happens to exist.

So the corrected principle:

> Uniqueness is `(binding, scope)`. A workspace's identity is its server UUID; git is the *preferred* binding, an explicit UUID link is the *fallback* binding, and the path hash is only a local default. Git-less projects are first-class — they just can't be auto-discovered, so they're joined by link, exactly like Vercel.
